description:
Château d'Island is an authentic 15th-century château at the transition from late-medieval to early-Renaissance architecture, set in the Morvan Regional Natural Park between Avallon and Vézelay. Notable historic interior features include its great salon and ceiling.

It's worth clarifying the name: "Island" here refers to the French commune of Island (part of Pontaubert), not the English word for a landmass surrounded by water. Today the property offers a mix of standard doubles/twins, superior doubles, and an "Apartment with Terrace" in the Maison du Cocher (coachman's house) — a separate building from the main château. Rooms feature garden views and soundproofing. It is a seasonal property, typically open from May through early November.

The château's position at the architectural transition between late-medieval and early-Renaissance styles gives it a genuinely layered character, reflecting the broader shift underway across French castle-building during the 15th century.

The coincidental placename "Island" — a French commune name unrelated to the English word — is worth stating plainly so prospective guests understand this is a landlocked Burgundy property, not a coastal or island destination.

The château's seasonal operating schedule, closing over the winter months, distinguishes it from most other properties in this collection that operate year-round.

The nearby Basilica of Vézelay, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, gives guests staying at Château d'Island easy access to one of Burgundy's most significant pilgrimage and architectural landmarks.

faqs.question: Is Château d'Island located on an actual island?
faqs.answer: No — "Island" is the name of the French commune (part of Pontaubert) where the château is located, not the English word for a landmass surrounded by water. The château is inland, in Burgundy's Morvan region.

faqs.question: Is Château d'Island open year-round?
faqs.answer: No — it's a seasonal property, typically open from May through early November. Check exact dates before booking.

faqs.question: Are all the accommodations at Château d'Island within the main building?
faqs.answer: No — most rooms are in the 15th-century main château, but the "Apartment with Terrace" is in the Maison du Cocher (coachman's house), a separate building on the estate.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** Between Avallon and Vézelay in Burgundy's Yonne department, within the Morvan Regional Natural Park; about 3.5-4 hours from Paris by car.

**Rooms & rates:** From €150/night — standard and superior rooms in the 15th-century main château, plus a separate Maison du Cocher (coachman's house) apartment with terrace.

**On-site:** Gastronomic restaurant and bar, park with outdoor seating, seminar/conference facilities, snooker table.

**Good to know:** Seasonal — typically open 1 May to early November only; check dates before booking. The Maison du Cocher apartment is a separate building from the historic château.

**Combine with:** The Basilica of Vézelay (UNESCO World Heritage), a short drive away.
